transcript:
[00:00] Priya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, um thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros then jump into what you all are trying to solve today.
[00:12] Alex (Mariner): hey hi, Alex here, head of platform at Mariner. We're evaluating Redwood for inference, mostly concerned about reliability and incident tolerance across our user-facing chat features.
[00:25] Priya: great, could you outline current stack and pain points? like where are you hosting models now and what's the trigger to look at Dedicated or Private?
[00:38] Dana (Mariner SRE): today we run a mix, some endpoints on OpenAI hosted, and some in-house smaller models on AWS EC2 GPUs. Pain points: noisy cold-starts, region failovers have been manual, and we hit throttles during peak events — we want automated fallbacks so UX doesn't degrade.
[00:56] Mark (Redwood SE): when you say fallbacks, do you mean both model fallback (like a smaller quantized model) and region fallback, or also downgrade to cached responses?
[01:06] Dana: all of the above, ideally. For customer-facing chat we want sub-300ms median response in NA, but on incidents we can tolerate up to 1 second as long as we don't return errors.
[01:19] Priya: ok that's helpful — what are your SLOs and error budgets today?
[01:24] Alex: we have an internal SLO of 99.9% availability for the chat API and p95 under 750ms, but that's aggressive during peak. We're exploring Dedicated to get predictability; also Private for regulated customers.
[01:38] Tina (Security): security wise we need SOC2 type II, SAML SSO for admin access, KMS integration for keys and audit logs. Also data residency for some EU customers.
[01:50] Mark: good, Redwood supports SOC2, SSO via SAML, and KMS/HSM integrations with the Private offering, and dedicated has VPC peering options. For Hosted we do bring-your-key via KMS for some enterprise tiers, but let me clarify exact flows after.
[02:08] Omar (Product): walk us through typical fallback policies you'd recommend — what does Redwood do out of the box?
[02:16] Mark: out of the box we have routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region-affinity, and custom fallback chains. Eg primary: Hosted high-capacity model in us-east; fallback 1: quantized variant with lower resource needs; fallback 2: cached answer or precomputed summary; fallback 3: degrade to synchronous retry with longer timeout.
[02:40] Alex: and multi-region? how automated is the failover if one region goes bad?
[02:45] Mark: there are two layers — control-plane routing that can automatically route by region health checks and client-side SDKs that respect sticky sessions. We also support cross-region cold-start mitigation with warm pools in secondary regions. But note, cold-starts for large models are non-trivial; we recommend warm-scaling.
[03:05] Dana: warm pools sound good, but that's extra cost. curious about cost vs reliability tradeoff — do you have guidance?
[03:12] Priya: absolutely — Redwood Optimize can run your traces and recommend warm pool sizes and batching to minimize incremental cost. Usually customers pin a minimal warm pool in a secondary region for critical endpoints and accept a slight latency bump. We can send a cost model.
[03:29] [00:03:30] Alex: during a region outage what's the expected client impact? like will requests fail over seamlessly or will sessions break?
[03:37] Mark: session stickiness can be preserved by syncing KV caches across regions for short windows; we have prefix KV cache replication but it's eventual. There may be some context loss for in-flight sessions, that's why we recommend saving conversational context client-side for failover or committing snapshots to object storage.
[03:57] Tina: is KV cache replication encrypted in transit and at rest?
[04:02] Mark: yes, encryption in transit and at rest. For Private deployments you manage keys via your KMS/HSM. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and customer-managed keys on enterprise tiers.
[04:15] [00:04:15] Dana: how about SLA — do you offer an uptime SLA for Hosted or Dedicated?
[04:21] Priya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; Hosted has published availability goals but full SLA is part of enterprise tier/contract. Typical Dedicated SLAs are 99.95% with prescribed incident response times.
[04:36] Alex: what about degradation policies — like automatic downgrade to a smaller model when load spikes?
[04:41] Mark: yes, policy-driven fallback chains allow automatic downgrade. You can define thresholds: if queueing or p95 crosses X, route new requests to a cheaper model or to async processing. We also support hedging and timeouts.
[04:56] Omar: latency vs cost — any empirical numbers? our chat is heavy on context length, lots of tokens.
[05:03] Mark: rough rule — 2x token cost for higher-capacity models vs quantized variants can be 3-5x cheaper but with some quality loss. We'll run benchmarks for your exact prompts. Also batching and KV cache reuse reduce cost significantly for repeated prefixes.
[05:20] [00:05:20] Tina: compliance — do you provide audit logs for admin actions and per-request logs for forensics?
[05:26] Aisha (CSM): yes, we provide detailed audit logs, per-route tracing, and can provide longer retention as an add-on for compliance needs.
[05:35] Dana: during incidents how does Redwood handle retries? are backoffs exponential, do you do circuit breakers?
[05:42] Mark: yes, built-in retry/backoff policies and service-level circuit breakers. You can plug in custom hooks to trigger fallbacks earlier based on custom metrics.
[05:52] Alex: curious about private deployments for regulated verticals — if we do on-prem, how much of fallback automation still works across regions?
[05:59] Mark: cross-site automation for on-prem is trickier — control plane can be deployed in a hybrid mode, but you may need networking peering and latency is a factor. We typically recommend Dedicated in multiple regions for global redundancy unless strict air-gap is required.
[06:16] [00:06:16] Omar: any real-world example of incident tolerance?
[06:19] Priya: yes — a fintech customer had a control-plane outage in one region; with multi-region routing + warm pools they automatically rerouted 92% of traffic with 200-600ms extra latency; for critical calls they had an async fallback that kept UX consistent. We can share a case study link.
[06:36] Dana: we want to understand the failure modes — e.g., model OOMs, kernel panics, networking blackholes — do you have recommended runbooks?
[06:45] Mark: we keep playbooks for common incidents — OOMs trigger graceful eviction to smaller batch sizes and start fallback chain; kernel-level failures trigger node drain and immediate reroute; networking blackholes are detected by health checks and circuit break. We'll share sanitized runbooks.
[07:02] Alex: what telemetry will we get in our console? token-level cost, per-route latency, traces, error types?
[07:09] Aisha: yes — Console includes token breakdown, per-model latency histograms, traces, and you can hook to Datadog or Splunk.
[07:17] [00:07:17] Tina: one more security Q — do you do annual pen tests and share reports?
[07:22] Priya: we perform regular pen tests and will share high-level reports; complete details under NDA.
[07:30] Dana: okay next, how long to set up a pilot to test failover? we want to simulate region outage and measure p95 and session continuity.
[07:37] Mark: typical pilot 2-4 weeks: week 1 onboarding and basic tests, week 2 synthetic load and failover scenarios. If you want Dedicated reserved pool for pilot that's extra provisioning but possible.
[07:50] Omar: on the SDK side any changes needed to support sticky sessions and retries?
[07:55] Mark: we have client SDKs that support automatic retries and route hints; for sticky context you may need to store session tokens and implement client-side reconnect. We'll provide code samples.
[08:06] [00:08:06] Alex: ok let's recap next steps — send security docs, pricing, run benchmarks, schedule deep dive.
[08:12] Priya: yes — I'll send SOC2, security whitepaper, and pricing later today. Mark will follow up with a proposed benchmark plan. Aisha will set up console access for the pilot account.
[08:21] Tina: can you include EU data residency proof for the Hosted option?
[08:25] Priya: yes we'll include region certification and data residency notes.
[08:30] Dana: last thing — do you offer contractual SLAs for Hosted?
[08:34] Priya: Hosted availability SLAs are available for enterprise customers — we'll include language in the contract estimate, but Dedicated gives more prescriptive uptime and latency SLOs.
[08:43] [00:08:43] Alex: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll identify three representative prompts and share them by monday.
[08:50] Priya: perfect, thanks — we'll follow up with the packet and schedule the SE deep dive.
[08:56] [00:08:56] Meeting end

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), filler words, and truncated sentences preserved to mimic raw Fireflies export. References: shared docs and links to SOC2, pricing sheet, and a previous fintech case study (links to be provided in follow up).
